# Dataset dictionary

**File:** `data/electricity_demand.csv`  
**Rows:** 8,760 hourly records for 2025  
**Data type:** Synthetic educational demonstration data generated by `data/generate_dataset.py` (fixed seed 42).

| Column | Meaning | Unit / values |
|---|---|---|
| `timestamp` | Hour represented by the record | YYYY-MM-DD HH:00:00 |
| `hour` | Hour of day | 0–23 |
| `day_of_week` | Day of week | 0=Monday through 6=Sunday |
| `is_weekend` | Whether the date is Saturday or Sunday | 0 or 1 |
| `temperature_c` | Ambient temperature | °C |
| `humidity_pct` | Relative humidity | % |
| `current_demand_mw` | Demand in the current hour | MW |
| `demand_lag_1h_mw` | Demand in the previous hour | MW |
| `rolling_mean_24h_mw` | Mean demand over the previous 24 hours | MW; previous observations only |
| `rolling_std_24h_mw` | Standard deviation over the previous 24 hours | MW; previous observations only |
| `spike_next_hour` | Prediction target | 1 if next-hour demand exceeds 110% of the previous 24-hour mean; otherwise 0 |

## Predictors used by the model

The model uses seven predictors: `hour`, `day_of_week`, `is_weekend`, `temperature_c`, `humidity_pct`, `current_demand_mw`, and `demand_lag_1h_mw`.

The app asks the user for hour, day of week, temperature, humidity and current demand. It derives `is_weekend` from the selected day and takes previous-hour demand from the latest dataset observation.

## Data limitations

This dataset is generated for an academic software demonstration. It is not measured by an electricity utility, does not represent a named grid or region, and should not be described as real-world observations. Mentor approval is still required for the dataset choice and project scope.
